title: Review how board proposals behave with several branches (dev, main, features)
notes: Today every proposal targets the repository's GitHub default branch only (proposals = pr, merge or direct, see docs/team-board.md).
The server checkout must match the default branch's backlog files, or the board answers 409; a checkout on dev or a feature branch refuses every proposal.
With a dev/main split the PR or commit lands on the default branch, not on dev; there is no per-repository target branch setting.
In merge and direct modes the default branch moves on every change, so the checkout goes stale until pulled; with several branches the backlog on dev and main can diverge.
Questions to settle: a target branch per repository, which branch the board reads, how a merge into dev reaches main, and whether the checkout should pull itself.
done_when: The branch behavior is decided, documented in docs/team-board.md and covered by tests, or a decision task records why it stays default-branch only
result: Review how board proposals behave with several branches (dev, main, features)
evidence: Decided: one target branch per repository (workspace 'branch', default = GitHub default branch); the board reads its checkout, which must be on that branch; reaching main from dev is the team's own merge; the checkout does not pull itself. Documented in docs/team-board.md 'Several branches'; tests/test_board_proposal_branch.py (pr and direct land on dev, fail without the change) and test_parse_repository_proposals.py; gate passed, doctor clean
